Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Pervasive Label Errors in Test Sets Destabilize Machine Learning Benchmarks (2103.14749v4) · paper method: The paper cautions that even unanimous five-worker corrections can be wrong. Its corrected-accuracy experiments remove unknown-label cases and correct only the consensus alternative-label set, so their noise-prevalence denominator differs from the initial fraction of validated label issues.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Pervasive Label Errors in Test Sets Destabilize Machine Learning Benchmarks (2103.14749v4) · paper method: Each screened example was independently shown to five MTurk workers choosing given label, predicted label, both or neither; an example counted as an error when fewer than three accepted the given label. Only random samples were checked for QuickDraw and Amazon Reviews; other flagged sets were fully checked.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Pervasive Label Errors in Test Sets Destabilize Machine Learning Benchmarks (2103.14749v4) · paper method: For the 50,000-image ILSVRC 2012 validation set used in place of unavailable ImageNet test labels, Table 1 reports 5,440 screened and checked examples, of which 2,916 met the five-worker validation rule, corresponding to 5.83% of that validation set; validated errors include ambiguity categories and are not all correctable single-label mistakes.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Pervasive Label Errors in Test Sets Destabilize Machine Learning Benchmarks (2103.14749v4) · paper method: The study uses confident learning with out-of-sample class probabilities and observed labels to screen likely benchmark errors before human review; its noise model assumes class-conditional noise, and for datasets without test splits the procedure uses cross-validation over the whole dataset.
